Choose the sentence that best completes the paragraph:

"Translators have long argued about whether to render a text literally or freely. A literal version preserves the original's structure but can read awkwardly; a free one reads well but may drift from what was actually said. ___"

options.markdown: Most working translators therefore treat the choice as a balance to be struck afresh in each passage.
Translation has existed for as long as written language itself.
Literal translation is clearly the more scholarly of the two approaches.
Many great works of literature have never been translated at all.

solutionMarkdown: The paragraph sets up a genuine two-sided tension, giving each side a cost. The completion must resolve that tension rather than pick a winner arbitrarily or change topic. Only the first does so; the third takes a side the paragraph deliberately left open.
